title: Cache Orchestrator: stochastic hit-curve projection and safe autodeploy for KV policies
creator: Asha Patel
body:
Summary:
Design and implement an automated recommendation and safe-apply flow for KV/prefix cache configurations focused on (1) stochastic hit-rate projection, (2) TTL and policy tuning suggestions that trade off cost vs latency, and (3) cache-key hygiene guidance. This ticket scopes the modeling, validation harness, rollout automation, and rollback budget calculation for safe autodeploys into Dedicated and Hosted environments.

Motivation:
We keep seeing ad-hoc cache config changes that either under-deliver savings or cause regressions in tail latency. Current guidance lives in spreadsheets and manual-run notebooks. We need a reproducible service that: (a) predicts prefix-level hit uplift for candidate keying/TTL changes under realistic sequence and burst distributions, (b) computes a conservative savings estimate and a probabilistic rollback budget, and (c) executes staged, observable config applies with automatic rollback triggers.

Goals (end state):
- A hit-projection model that takes historical prefix traces and outputs median/90/99 hit uplift and variance for proposed config deltas.
- Policy tuner that recommends per-prefix TTLs and key canonicalization rules with expected cost reduction and expected increase in requests served from origin.
- Safe autodeploy orchestrator that performs shadow validation, micro-canary applies, metrics gating and automated rollbacks using a probabilistic change detector.

Proposed approach:
1) Modeling: build a stochastic simulator that ingests recent request traces (sequence lengths, prefix frequencies, inter-arrival times) and replays them under candidate policies. Core model components:
   - Prefix frequency histogram + time-decayed windowing (to capture drift).
   - KV hit model that accounts for batching-dependent lookup collapse: simulate batching windows and cache key collisions.
   - TTL semantics: support fixed TTL, sliding-ttl and adaptive decays (exponential backoff) with configurable refresh behaviors.
   - Noise model for sampling uncertainty; fit a Bayesian posterior over hit-rate uplift so we can produce credible intervals.

2) Policy compiler: translate recommendations into declarative config diffs consumable by runtime: cache-key transforms, TTL map, and per-route cache mode (readonly, readthrough, prefetch). Include a linter to detect high-risk transforms (e.g., high cardinality sharding, user-sensitive fields).

3) Validation harness: offline shadow-run mode where we shadow apply config to a subset of traffic and compute real-world hit/loss vs simulator prediction. Also run synthetic microburst stress tests to estimate tail latency under degraded cache scenarios.

4) Safe autodeploy flow: staged steps with automatic abort/rollback criteria:
   - Dry-run -> Shadow -> Canary 0.1% -> Ramp (1%, 5%, 20%) -> Full apply.
   - At each stage use Bayesian online change detection on key metrics: origin RPS, p99 tail latency, error rate, and per-prefix hit variance. If posterior probability of regression > 95% for two consecutive 1-min windows, auto-roll back.

Data & metrics:
- Inputs: per-request prefix, route, tokens_generated, request_latency, batch_size, model_variant, region.
- Outputs: predicted hit uplift percentiles, estimated per-million-token cost delta, expected origin request delta, rollback budget (max allowed extra origin RPS) and confidence interval.
- Metrics tracked during rollouts: per-prefix hit, origin RPS, token cost delta, p50/p95/p99 latency, model errors.

Rollout safety budget (novelty):
Compute a probabilistic rollback budget B such that P(origin RPS increase > B) < alpha (alpha default 0.05) under the posterior. Use B to set Canary caps and to compute cost-savings floor for alerting. This lets us revert early if the observed origin increase exceeds B.

Acceptance criteria (high level):
- Simulator exists and produces credible interval predictions that match shadow-run outcomes within tolerances (median within 10%, 90th percentile within 20%).
- Policy compiler produces a config diff and linter warnings for high-risk changes.
- Autodeploy flow integrated with Console feature flags: ability to trigger staged rollout and automatic rollback.
- Runbook for operators and playbook for SREs describing how to override/force rollback.

Operational notes:
- Start with low-risk prefixes (high frequency, low cardinality) to build trust.
- Maintain a shadow-sample baseline for at least 48–72 hours after full apply.
- Provide an explainability output per recommendation ("why this prefix gets TTL reduced") referencing top contributing examples from traces.

Deliverables:
- Prototype simulator code + Jupyter notebooks (internal)
- Service endpoint that accepts candidate config and returns hit uplift distribution and rollback budget
- Policy compiler + linter + config diff UI in Console
- Autodeploy orchestration and rollback hooks
comments: 2026-02-17 - Marcus Chen: Kickoff sync with SRE and Runtime teams. Agreed to use 14-day rolling windows for training traces and to exclude PII routes. Action: I will prototype the simulator using existing telemetry samples (ENG-420801 traces).

2026-02-24 - Asha Patel: Simulator spike done. Initial stochastic replay shows promising separation between candidate TTLs on toy datasets. Observed that batching increases apparent hit ratios by ~12% when batch size > 8. NOTE: need to account for client-side batching behavior variability.

2026-03-02 - Lena Ortiz (SRE): Ran shadow-run for 48h on 3 low-risk prefixes. Shadow hit uplift matched simulator median within 8%. Logged dashboard: https://redwood-internal.dashboards/prefix-shadow-ENG-445217
2026-03-05 - Design review (Diego Ramos): UX for explainability panel reviewed. We decided to show top-5 contributing query examples and an "undo" button in the Console rollout panel.
2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen: Built canary orchestration prototype and smoke-tested rollback trigger. Need product signoff on default alpha and canary ramp schedule.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator credible intervals validated against 48h shadow-run for 3 pilot prefixes.
Policy compiler emits config diffs with human-readable rationale and linter warnings for risky transforms.
Autodeploy stages execute with automatic rollback when posterior regression probability > 95% for 2 consecutive windows.
Operational runbook and SRE override controls present in Console before enabling >20% traffic ramps.
steps: Implement stochastic simulator service and notebook artifacts (owner: Marcus).
Create policy compiler that outputs config diffs and linter warnings (owner: Eng-Platform team).
Integrate shadow-run harness with telemetry pipeline; run initial 48h experiments on low-risk prefixes (owner: SRE).
Implement autodeploy orchestration with metrics gating + Bayesian online change detector (owner: Marcus/Lena).
Design Console UI for recommendation review, explainability and staged rollout controls (owner: Design).
Document runbook and escalation paths; train support/solutions engineering on how to interpret rollback budgets.
notes: Trade-offs: conservative posteriors reduce potential savings but improve safety. We will iterate alpha for rollback sensitivity with real-world data.
We intentionally avoid fully automated aggressive global applies for first 2 quarters. Focus on recommending and automating low-risk prefixes.
Privacy: all traces used exclude user identifiers; route-level hashing is performed prior to storage per compliance guidance.
Edge cases: very high-cardinality prefixes should default to "readonly" cache mode; prefetch and pre-warm are out of scope for initial rollout.
